children: A reading of the U.S. labor market from The Conference Board moved up in August, with signs that underemployment is easing and perceptions of job availability are improving, a gauge of employment showed.
The Employment Trends Index, or ETI, rose to 108.53, from an upwardly revised 107.76 in July.

The move continues a rebound that started last month after declines in May and June and brings the index up 2% higher than where it was a year ago, said Conrad Qi, an economic data scientist associate at The Conference Board.

The index is a forward-looking measure for payrolls, and when it increases, employment is on track to grow as well. All eight of the index's components have delivered positive average contributions over the past six months, though they were mixed in August, Qi said.

The largest contributions came from declines in the ratio of involuntarily part-time to all part-time workers, along with the share of consumers reporting that jobs are harder to get. Those shifts suggest less underemployment and better perceptions of job availability, according to Qi.
Employment in temporary help services increased in August, and industrial production ticked up.

The biggest drag on the index was initial claims for unemployment insurance, though claims remained below their June level, indicating only a modest pickup in layoffs. The percentage of small firms with positions they weren't able to fill fell, but remained more elevated than usual, Qi said.

title: U.S. Employment Trends Index Rose in August, Conference Board Says
